rule.title: Requirement of Just Cause to Terminate Tenancy
rule.requirement: An owner shall not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice to terminate after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months. If additional adult tenants are added before an existing tenant reaches 24 months of occupancy, just cause applies only if all tenants have occupied for at least 12 months or at least one tenant has occupied for at least 24 months.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months, or, if additional adult tenants were added before an existing tenant reached 24 months, once all tenants have occupied for 12+ months or at least one tenant has occupied for 24+ months.
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy is exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(1); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in a nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, licensed residential care facility for the elderly, or adult residential facility are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(2); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(3); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in which the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with the owner who maintains their principal residence at the residential real property are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(4); document-wide]; Single-family owner-occupied residences in which the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms (including an ADU or junior ADU), or a mobilehome, are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(5); document-wide]; A duplex in which the owner occupied one of the units as their principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues occupancy (where neither unit is an ADU or junior ADU) is exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(6); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless the housing is a mobilehome) is exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(7); document-wide]; Separately alienable residential real property (including a mobilehome) is exempt from this section if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, corporate-member LLC, or mobilehome park management, and the tenant has been provided the required statutory written exemption disclosure notice. rule.title: No-Fault Just Cause: Owner or Relative Occupancy
rule.requirement: An owner may terminate a tenancy for no-fault just cause if the owner or the owner's spouse, domestic partner, children, grandchildren, parents, or grandparents intend to occupy the residential property as their primary residence for at least 12 continuous months. rule.title: No-Fault Just Cause: Withdrawal from Rental Market
rule.requirement: An owner may terminate a tenancy for no-fault just cause to withdraw the residential real property from the rental market.
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy is exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(1); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in a nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, licensed residential care facility for the elderly, or adult residential facility are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(2); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(3); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in which the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with the owner who maintains their principal residence at the residential real property are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(4); document-wide]; Single-family owner-occupied residences in which the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms (including an ADU or junior ADU), or a mobilehome, are exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(5); document-wide]; A duplex in which the owner occupied one of the units as their principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues occupancy (where neither unit is an ADU or junior ADU) is exempt from this section. [§ 1946.2(e)(6); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless the housing is a mobilehome) is exempt from this section.
